title: "Simple validation examples"

vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Simple validation examples}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Each example below explains one comparison and prints a numeric table with
package value, reference value, and their difference. Values near zero in the
difference column indicate numerical agreement. All code runs directly here.
There are no external validation files or test runners. Base R supplies the
references, except for `sandwich` in the optional HC checks and the package's
existing `boot` dependency. These checks establish agreement for the displayed
examples, not coverage under all conditions. Knitting executes and prints the examples.

The primary reference is Bulus (2026), especially Table 1 and Appendices A1-A2.
Observation weighting is an implementation extension and is checked separately.

```{r setup}
library(hcttest)
```

## Student test: compare with t.test()

Use the same two groups in the remaining mean-difference comparisons. The
constant-variance result should match base R's equal-variance t test.

```{r student}
x <- c(1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10)
y <- c(0, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 11, 14)
fit <- hct.test(x, y, method = "student", verbose = FALSE)
reference <- t.test(x, y, var.equal = TRUE)
comparison <- data.frame(
  metric = c("Difference", "SE", "t", "df", "p", "Lower", "Upper"),
  package = unlist(fit$test[1, c("delta", "se", "t", "df", "p", "lcl", "ucl")], use.names = FALSE),
  reference = c(mean(x)-mean(y), reference$stderr, unname(reference$statistic),
                unname(reference$parameter), reference$p.value, reference$conf.int))
comparison$difference <- comparison$package - comparison$reference
print(comparison, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Welch test: compare with t.test()

Here the SE allows unequal group variances, and the df use Welch-Satterthwaite.

```{r welch}
fit <- hct.test(x, y, method = "hc2", df = "welch-satterthwaite", verbose = FALSE)
reference <- t.test(x, y)
comparison <- data.frame(
  metric = c("SE", "t", "df", "p"),
  package = unlist(fit$test[1, c("se", "t", "df", "p")], use.names = FALSE),
  reference = c(reference$stderr, unname(reference$statistic),
                unname(reference$parameter), reference$p.value))
comparison$difference <- comparison$package - comparison$reference
print(comparison, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Per-observation weights: compare Student SE with lm()

`weights` is a weight for each observation. The separate `mixnorm.weight`
argument in summary-distribution calculations refers to mixture proportions.
The indicator is one for the first group, keeping the difference x minus y.

```{r weighted-student}
dat <- data.frame(value = c(x, y), first = c(rep(1, length(x)), rep(0, length(y))),
                  w = c(1, 2, 1, 3, 2, 1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1))
model <- lm(value ~ first, data = dat, weights = w)
fit <- hct.test(x, y, weights = dat$w, method = "student", verbose = FALSE)
comparison <- data.frame(
  metric = c("Difference", "SE"),
  package = c(fit$test$delta, fit$test$se),
  reference = c(unname(coef(model)["first"]), sqrt(vcov(model)["first", "first"])))
comparison$difference <- comparison$package - comparison$reference
print(comparison, row.names = FALSE)
```

## HC reference comparisons

The next checks use the same weighted data and model. Each compares one HC SE
with `sandwich::vcovHC()`, without introducing a new variance formula. If the
suggested package sandwich is absent, that comparison is explicitly skipped;
install it and knit again to run the check. Successful Student/Welch checks do
not imply these skipped comparisons passed.

### HC0

HC0 uses the unadjusted squared residual scores.

```{r hc0}
if (requireNamespace("sandwich", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- hct.test(x, y, weights = dat$w, method = "hc0", verbose = FALSE)
  reference_se <- sqrt(sandwich::vcovHC(model, type = "HC0")["first", "first"])
  comparison <- data.frame(
    metric = "SE",
    package = fit$test$se,
    reference = reference_se)
  comparison$difference <- comparison$package - comparison$reference
  print(comparison, row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  message("HC0 comparison skipped: install sandwich to run it.")
}
```

```{r hc1}

```

## Normal-approximation raw p value

When ci = "z", the two-sided p value is twice the upper standard-normal tail
of abs(delta/SE). This uses the same SE as the raw normal interval.

```{r z-raw}
fit <- hct.test(x, y, method = "hc3", ci = "z", verbose = FALSE)
reference_p <- 2 * pnorm(abs(fit$test$delta / fit$test$se), lower.tail = FALSE)
comparison <- data.frame(
  metric = "Normal p",
  package = fit$test$p,
  reference = reference_p)
comparison$difference <- comparison$package - comparison$reference
print(comparison, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Standardized difference and its normal p value

Check the effect-size point estimate against the manually pooled SD. The SMD
normal test uses d divided by its own SE, so it need not equal the raw p value.
This example does not independently validate the SMD SE approximation.

```{r smd}
fit <- hct.test(x, y, method = "hc3", verbose = FALSE)
smd <- robust.smd(fit, ci = "z", verbose = FALSE)
pooled_sd <- sqrt(((length(x) - 1) * var(x) + (length(y) - 1) * var(y)) /
                  (length(x) + length(y) - 2))
reference_d <- (mean(x) - mean(y)) / pooled_sd
reference_p <- 2 * pnorm(abs(smd$es$d / smd$es$se), lower.tail = FALSE)
comparison <- data.frame(
  metric = c("d", "Normal p"),
  package = c(smd$es$d, smd$es$p),
  reference = c(reference_d, reference_p))
comparison$difference <- comparison$package - comparison$reference
print(comparison, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Unweighted trimming: compare the retained mean with base R

The existing convention removes round(n * trim) observations from each tail.
Here ten observations with trim = 0.1 retain values 2 through 9.

```{r trimming}
fit <- hct.test(1:10, 3:12, trim = 0.1, verbose = FALSE)
comparison <- data.frame(
  metric = c("Trimmed mean", "Retained n"),
  package = c(fit$parms$m1, fit$parms$n1),
  reference = c(mean(2:9), length(2:9)))
comparison$difference <- comparison$package - comparison$reference
print(comparison, row.names = FALSE)
```

## g-and-h generation: check the transformation directly

The normal draws are sample-standardized, transformed, and rescaled to preserve
their realized sample mean and SD. With nonzero shapes this sample calibration
introduces dependence within a sample; it is not an analytically calibrated
independent population generator. Shapes are only accepted with a normal base.

```{r g-and-h}
set.seed(12)
normal <- gendat.hct.test(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 40, 60)
set.seed(12)
shaped <- gendat.hct.test(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 40, 60, norm.transform.g = 0.3, norm.tranform.h = 0.1)
z <- (normal$y1 - mean(normal$y1)) / sd(normal$y1)
t <- expm1(0.3 * z) / 0.3 * exp(0.1 * z^2 / 2)
reference <- mean(normal$y1) + sd(normal$y1) * (t - mean(t)) / sd(t)
comparison <- data.frame(
  metric = c("Value 1", "Value 2", "Mean", "SD"),
  package = c(shaped$y1[1:2], mean(shaped$y1), sd(shaped$y1)),
  reference = c(reference[1:2], mean(normal$y1), sd(normal$y1)))
comparison$difference <- comparison$package - comparison$reference
print(comparison, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Study rows: compare with a direct calculation

The helper should reproduce a direct calculation for each study. We compare the
estimate and its variance. The SMD normal p value is checked separately above.
No pooled model is fitted.

```{r study-table}
studies <- data.frame(m1 = c(1, 2), m2 = c(0.5, 1.5), sd1 = c(1, 1.2),
                      sd2 = c(1.1, 1.5), n1 = c(30, 40), n2 = c(35, 45))
results <- meta.robust.smd(studies, method = "hc2", ci = "z", pool = FALSE)
fit <- hct.test(m1 = 1, m2 = 0.5, sd1 = 1, sd2 = 1.1, n1 = 30, n2 = 35,
                method = "hc2", verbose = FALSE)
direct <- robust.smd(fit, ci = "z", verbose = FALSE)
comparison <- data.frame(
  metric = c("Effect", "Variance"),
  package = c(results$yi[1], results$vi[1]),
  reference = c(direct$es$d, direct$es$se^2))
comparison$difference <- comparison$package - comparison$reference
print(comparison, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Multiple outcomes: compare one row with a direct analysis

Outcome-specific missing-data removal can give different analyzed sample sizes.
Rows remain separate; no multiple-testing adjustment or covariance model is added.

```{r multiple-outcomes}
participants <- data.frame(group = factor(rep(c("A", "B"), c(6, 8))),
                           outcome1 = c(x, y), outcome2 = c(x, y) * 2)
participants$outcome2[1] <- NA_real_
results <- multi.robust.smd(participants, c("outcome1", "outcome2"), "group",
                            method = "hc3", na.rm = TRUE, ci = "z")
fit <- hct.test(x, y, method = "hc3", verbose = FALSE)
direct <- robust.smd(fit, ci = "z", verbose = FALSE)
comparison <- data.frame(
  metric = c("Outcome 1 effect", "Outcome 1 variance", "Outcome 2 first-group n"),
  package = c(results$yi[1], results$vi[1], results$n1[2]),
  reference = c(direct$es$d, direct$es$se^2, sum(!is.na(participants$outcome2[participants$group == "A"]))))
comparison$difference <- comparison$package - comparison$reference
print(comparison, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Ordinary bootstrap: compare with boot()

Use the same seed, group strata, and simple pooled-SD statistic in both calls.
This validates resampling and the resulting SEs for an untrimmed example; it is
not a coverage study. A small replicate count keeps the example quick.

```{r bootstrap}
set.seed(20)
bdat <- data.frame(y = c(rnorm(30), rnorm(40, 0.5)),
                   group = factor(rep(c("A", "B"), c(30, 40))))
statistic <- function(data, indices) {
  sample <- data[indices, ]
  a <- sample$y[sample$group == "A"]
  b <- sample$y[sample$group == "B"]
  pooled <- sqrt(((length(a)-1)*var(a) + (length(b)-1)*var(b)) /
                 (length(a)+length(b)-2))
  c(mean(a)-mean(b), (mean(a)-mean(b))/pooled)
}
set.seed(21)
reference <- boot::boot(bdat, statistic, R = 199, strata = bdat$group)
set.seed(21)
result <- boot.hct.test(y ~ group, bdat, boot.rep = 199, parallel = "no",
                        ncpus = 1, verbose = FALSE)
comparison <- data.frame(
  metric = c("Observed difference", "Observed d", "Difference SE", "d SE"),
  package = c(result$est.data, result$se.boot),
  reference = c(reference$t0, apply(reference$t, 2, sd)))
comparison$difference <- comparison$package - comparison$reference
print(comparison, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Power: compare with the noncentral t distribution

The noncentrality, df, alpha, and tail convention are specified directly; this
checks the calculation rather than interpreting observed power as prospective.

```{r power}
# With 30 observations per group, this planned effect gives ncp = 2.
fit <- power.hct.test(
  d = 2 * sqrt(2 / 30),
  n2 = 30,
  method = "constant",
  claim.basis = "md.pval",
  test.distribution = "t",
  verbose = 0
)

critical <- qt(0.975, df = 58)
reference <- pt(-critical, df = 58, ncp = 2) +
  pt(critical, df = 58, ncp = 2, lower.tail = FALSE)

print(data.frame(
  metric = "Power",
  package = fit$power,
  reference = reference,
  difference = fit$power - reference
), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Scope and reference

The companion study-tables vignette preserves the supplied 29-row dataset and
shows unnormalized inverse-variance weights calculated from our current formulas.
These examples do not externally validate weighted SMD variances or establish
bootstrap coverage.
Unsupported analytical weighted trimming remains disabled. Internal Lambda-prime
helpers are not part of the public interface.

Bulus, M. (2026). Robust standard errors and confidence intervals for standardized
mean difference. *Research Synthesis Methods*. Advance online publication.

## Plot confidence intervals

The following comparisons check that the plotted SMD bands match direct
robust.smd calculations at alpha = 0.05 and alpha = 0.01. The summaries,
small-sample correction and scaling settings are identical. Plot output is
returned invisibly as a data frame; each table reports numbers and differences.

### Normal plot bands

```{r plot-bands-z, fig.show='hide'}
fit95 <- hct.test(m1 = 0.5, m2 = 0, sd1 = 1, sd2 = 1.4,
                   n1 = 35, n2 = 45, method = "hc2",
                   alpha = 0.05, verbose = FALSE)
fit99 <- fit95
fit99$parms$alpha <- 0.01
smd95 <- robust.smd(fit95, ci = "z", ss.adjust = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
smd99 <- robust.smd(fit99, ci = "z", ss.adjust = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
bands <- plot(smd95, pretty = TRUE)
reference <- c(smd95$es$lcl, smd95$es$ucl, smd99$es$lcl, smd99$es$ucl)
plotted <- unlist(bands[c("lower95", "upper95", "lower99", "upper99")],
                  use.names = FALSE)
data.frame(limit = c("95 lower", "95 upper", "99 lower", "99 upper"),
           plotted = plotted, reference = reference,
           difference = plotted - reference)
```

### Central-t plot bands

### Bootstrap replay at alpha = 0.01

This comparison reruns the original bootstrap at alpha = 0.01, using the
same data, arguments and starting seed. The plot performs the same replay
internally. Its 99 percent percentile limits should match the direct call.

```{r bootstrap-plot-replay, fig.show='hide'}
replay.data <- data.frame(
  group = factor(rep(c("A", "B"), each = 30)),
  outcome = c(seq(-1.3, 1.7, length.out = 30),
              seq(-1.2, 1.6, length.out = 30)))
set.seed(2026)
original.boot <- boot.hct.test(outcome ~ group, data = replay.data,
                               alpha = 0.05, boot.rep = 999,
                               parallel = "no", ncpus = 1, verbose = FALSE)
plotted.boot <- plot(original.boot, pretty = TRUE, boot.ci = "percentile")
set.seed(2026)
direct.boot99 <- boot.hct.test(outcome ~ group, data = replay.data,
                               alpha = 0.01, boot.rep = 999,
                               parallel = "no", ncpus = 1, verbose = FALSE)
index <- which(direct.boot99$est.type == "Standardized")
reference <- c(direct.boot99$lcl.boot.perc[index], direct.boot99$ucl.boot.perc[index])
plotted <- c(plotted.boot$lower99, plotted.boot$upper99)
data.frame(limit = c("99 lower", "99 upper"), plotted = plotted,
           reference = reference, difference = plotted - reference)
```
